question: A grants officer has a draft that is right in structure and evidence, but its second section is too technical for her readers. What is the most efficient next step?
options: A) Rewrite her original request to mention the reader's level, and ask for the whole document to be produced again.
B) Accept the draft as it stands and rewrite the technical section herself before the document goes any further.
C) Ask for three alternative versions of the whole document, and choose whichever of them reads most accessibly.
D) Ask for the second section to be rewritten for a non-specialist reader, leaving the rest of the draft as it is.
correct_answers: D) Ask for the second section to be rewritten for a non-specialist reader, leaving the rest of the draft as it is.
explanations: Regenerating everything puts the sections she was happy with back at risk, and she then has to re-review the whole document.
Rewriting it herself is a reasonable fallback, but doing it before asking for a revision gives up the cheapest improvement available.
Producing three full alternatives multiplies the reading and comparison work to fix a problem confined to one section.
Correct. Only one part is wrong, so only that part needs to change. A targeted revision keeps the structure and evidence she has already accepted, and it makes the improvement easy to check.
